title: Design of Low-Power Digitally Controlled Oscillator for All-Digital PLL Receiver in Zero-Energy IoT Devices
authors: J. A. M. Agito; X. Zhu; J. A. Hora; H. Mohammad
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in the era of sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication demands ultra-low power and high-frequency circuit solutions to support sustainable, near-zero energy operation. As IoT devices become more ubiquitous in applications such as smart environments, industrial automation, and wearable electronics, there is a growing need for compact and energy-efficient frequency generators capable of operating in the millimeter-wave spectrum. This study presents the design and analysis of a Digitally Controlled Oscillator (DCO) operating at 45 GHz, conforming to the IEEE 802.11aj standard, and implemented using GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted Silicon-On-Insulator (FD-SOI) technology. The oscillator core adopts a complementary Colpitts topology, chosen for its efficiency and suitability at high frequencies. Frequency tuning is achieved through a digitally controlled switched capacitor array, implemented with lowleakage transmission gates. Operating at a low supply voltage of 0.8 V, the proposed DCO achieves a power consumption of only 5.959 mW and demonstrates excellent spectral purity, with a phase noise of −99.03 dBc/Hz at 1 MHz offset, making it ideal for ultra-low-power mmWave receivers in dense IoT networks.

title: MAGNET: An optimized DevOps framework for efficient software integration and orchestration in the IoT-Edge-Cloud Continuum
authors: E. Agorogiannis; K. Petrakis; G. Antonopoulos; T. Anagnostopoulos; N. Grigoropoulos; Z. Benomar
abstract: This paper introduces MAGNET, a DevOps framework comprising Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment practices, alongside flexible development and integration infrastructures, as applied in COGNIFOG, an innovative computing ecosystem currently under development that uses decentralized decision making, machine learning, and distributed computing to enhance autonomy, adaptability, and scalability within the IoT-edge-cloud continuum. This work demonstrates the efficiency and adaptability of the COGNIFOG ecosystem through three real-world trials in smart cities, e-health, and smart manufacturing, along with the creation of a comprehensive QuickStart Guide for deployment, offering a robust solution for the complexities of next-generation computing environments.

title: A Machine Learning Framework for Detecting and Mitigation of Cyber Threats in IoT Environments
authors: K. M. R. Seetharaman; P. Yadav
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning are becoming more and more important in enhancing threat detection, response, and proactive defense as cybersecurity quickly changes. Two prominent solutions, leverage ML to solve Cybect Threat Intelligence (CTI) issues. A machine learningbased approach for identifying and reducing cyber threats in IoT settings is presented in this research, with an emphasis on the categorization of cyberattacks using the ResNet model. The framework is evaluated employing the CICDS 2019 dataset, and the ResNet model outperforms traditional machine learning models such as Feedforward Neural Network (FFNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), achieving an accuracy of 99.5% and an AUC of 93.3%. Although it achieved high accuracy, the discriminatory power of the ResNet model is less than optimum, as seen from the ROC plot; more work needs to be done. This paper has shown how DL can be applied effectively to IoT cyber threat detection and proposes research and development areas for enhancement, such as different data sets, tuning models of DL, and light models in the IoT environment.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Next Generation IoT Infrastructure: Challenges and Opportunities
authors: R. Arabelli; D. K. Chotaliya; R. T. Gadhave; B. Haritha; L. C. Kasireddy; M. Soni
abstract: Numerous facets of the public realm could be revolutionised by the convergence of the Internet of Things (the Internet of Things) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This project developed a based-on data predictive maintenance system for manufacturing production lines. One of these anticipated improvements that can be included into the factory's production system is “AI of Things (AIoT),” which refers to the use of the IoT to carry out intelligent tasks with the aid of AI integration. By using the information created by IoT sensors progressively, the system utilizes machine learning (ML), a part of AI, to recognize expected blunders preceding they happen. The viability of the innovation was surveyed utilizing IoT information from genuine assembling frameworks, and the results of the appraisal demonstrated that the prescient support structure was effective in distinguishing potential failure indicators and could assist with forestalling some production stops. Comparing the performance of ML techniques revealed that frameworks of the bagging ensemble technique Random Forest and the boosting technique XGBoost appeared to outperform each of the techniques in the assessment. The factory's production system now uses the best-performing ML techniques from the present research.

title: Digital Twin-Driven Testing of IoT Systems: A Scalable Simulation-Based Approach
authors: G. Georgiev; R. Trifonov; D. Gotseva; G. Kotov
abstract: Digital twins are emerging as a transformative approach for testing Internet of Things (IoT) systems, offering virtual replicas of physical environments to enhance test efficiency, scalability, and reliability. This paper presents a scalable simulation-based testing methodology driven by digital twin technology. We discuss how a digital twin of a smart home IoT system can be used to execute extensive test scenarios faster and more safely than on physical hardware. A hypothetical experimental evaluation is described in which a smart home digital twin is subjected to various sensor events, network conditions, and fault injections. Comparative analysis with traditional physical testing shows significant improvements: test coverage is broadened by simulating extreme and rare conditions, and testing time is greatly reduced through accelerated and parallelized virtual experiments. The results indicate that digital twin-driven testing can uncover 30% more faults prior to deployment and reduce testing duration by over 40% compared to conventional methods.

title: Comparative Study of Clouds Services integrated with DevOps Practices
authors: P. Gupta; S. Bhatia
abstract: In today’s world, where everything is revolving around cloud that provides in-demand services of any industry, corporates or Institutions. DevOps refers to the combination of the development as well as the operations in a shared and collaborative way for the work done by an organization’s application development and the IT operations teams. The significance of the paper includes comparative analysis of different industries where the cloud and DevOps can be integrated that helps to take the author’s research to the next level in the real-time environment. This paper presents comparative study on enhancing the clouds services by using DevOps practices that helps to save money, increases speed, security aspects and provides flexibility and scalability. With CloudOps, services are cost efficient, accessible and seamlessly integrated. Also the paper demonstrates the deployment of matrices based on DevOps, AWS and Azure Effectiveness that helps in understanding how well DevOps suit with various platforms.

title: Emerging IOT Cybersecurity Threats in Machine Learning
authors: V. R. Chintha; S. K. R. Akkemgari; V. N. R. K. Nizampatnam; R. Kaur; M. Sudagar
abstract: The development of Internet of Things (IOT) devices has led to new danger routes in our connected society in recent years. Meagre IoT security practices make all these devices interesting targets for attackers, even though they bring automation and real-time feedback. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of how to detect and mitigate cybersecurity threats in IoT, leveraging statistical anomaly detection with machine learning (ML) techniques. A combination of the RF (Random Forest) technique and packet size analysis to detect unusual behaviours and classify them as network intrusions was employed. Additionally, a CIAE risk matrix was applied to estimate the exposure degree of device-level vulnerabilities. That item stands for CIAE or confidentiality, integrity, availability and exploitability. On benchmark datasets, the recommended technique beat traditional models with 96.3% accuracy and 0.98 AUC. These results suggest combining strategies to improve IoT cybersecurity.

title: Prediction of DevOps readiness for software organization based on machine learning
authors: Z. N. Hasan; I. A. Saleh
abstract: The term “DevOps predictions” is used in this paper only to refer to the ability to predict DevOps adoption maturity in software organizations. The paper presents a machine learning model for predicting the level of DevOps adoption maturity in software companies. This model assesses readiness based on three key dimensions: cultural alignment, technical infrastructure, and operational resilience. This method enables an organization’s overall ability to adequately deploy and maintain DevOps practices. This paper presents a machine learning-powered pipeline for predicting DevOps readiness in software companies, helping support strategic planning and digital transformation. The proposed method boasts high predictive power and reliability thanks to the application of several ensemble learning techniques and, most importantly, a voting regression model. The model’s $\mathbf{R}$-SQ coefficient was 0.99, and its error statistics were very low (MAE $=0.04$, RMSE $=0.04$), demonstrating the model’s high effectiveness in predicting organizational patterns and readiness indicators. The research combines technical performance analysis and an implementation-based tool to measure DevOps maturity. These findings suggest that machine learning can improve decision-making and guide organizations toward more successful DevOps adoption.

title: A Scalable DevOps Framework Using Kubernetes-Orchestrated Microservices for Cloud-Native Infrastructure
authors: S. S. Poojary; S. Kamble; G. S. Mamatha
abstract: Think of a Formula 1 pit crew, swapping tires and tuning aerodynamics in seconds, guided by a race engineer's precise commands. That's the heart of our cloud-native DevOps framework, leveraging Kubernetes to orchestrate microservices for fast, reliable, and sustainable applications. This paper presents an innovative approach that empowers teams with automated CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, observability, fault tolerance, security, AI-driven optimization, multi-cloud strategies, carbon-aware scheduling, regulatory compliance, cultural transformation, and a DevOps maturity model. By harnessing Kubernetes' pods, services, and autoscaling, we deliver scalability, resilience, and efficiency. Through clear architectural insights, real-world e-commerce and IoT case studies, and unique metrics, we tackle challenges like network performance, security, cost, sustainability, compliance, and team collaboration, providing a practical blueprint for modern DevOps practitioners.

title: AI-Augmented Compiler Optimization for Energyefficient Software Execution on Embedded Systems
authors: S. K. Malaraju; S. K. Madishetty
abstract: The recent trend of the increased usage of embedded systems (such as IoT, autonomous devices, and edge computing) is associated with the increased demand to have energy-efficient software that does not impact performance. The traditional compiler optimization strategies, which are extremely useful in the case of generic workloads, are not likely to be able to respond to the dynamic energy and performance needs of a heterogeneous embedded system. The study examines AI-enhanced compiler optimization systems that use machine learning and reinforcement learning in improving the code generation, pass ordering, and runtime tuning with energy efficiency. The study shows that energy consumption can be drastically reduced without compromising the performance and accuracy of the systems based on multiple architectures through the combination of predictive cost models, reinforcement-based heuristics, and domain-specific auto-schedulers. Other areas of study that the research identifies that allow cross-layer co-optimization include compiler-guided dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) and accuracy-conscious intermediate representations. The accuracy of the proposed approach is confirmed in the experimental results of benchmark suites like BEEBS and Embench, which demonstrate a steady increase in code quality and energy efficiency relative to traditional approaches based on heuristics. The work is useful to the intelligent compiler design that has been evolving as it provides a pathway in the direction of sustainable as well as adaptive and portable. optimization strategies of the nextgeneration embedded systems.

title: Comprehensive Study of Data Centric and DevOps Algorithms Based Cloud Security
authors: S. R. Goli; G. Deshpande; R. Konda; A. K. R. Goli
abstract: Cloud security is essential for safeguarding sensitive and critical data while ensuring reliable operation within a computing setup where tasks are distributed and processed by multiple interconnected nodes. It protects data, applications, and infrastructure associated with cloud computing and is designed to secure the cloud environment from cyberattacks, unauthorized access, and related threats. This study elaborates on two primary approaches to cloud security: data-centric and DevOps-based techniques. Data-centric strategies focus on securing the data itself through advanced encryption and secure key management. DevOps-based security integrates protection mechanisms into the software development lifecycle, promoting early detection of vulnerabilities. The paper explores various techniques such as dynamic AES, RSA, blockchain-based key management, and automated policy enforcement frameworks such as SARIK. Each method's advantages and limitations are analyzed, offering a comparative perspective. The overall study demonstrates that combining both approaches improves security effectiveness and addresses ongoing challenges in cloud environments.

title: AI-Powered CNC Digital Twin for Predictive Maintenance
authors: S. Singh; S. Sethi; R. Sharma; D. Vaibhavi; A. Tiwari
abstract: In today’s manufacturing landscape, maintaining the operational efficiency of CNC (Computer Numerical Control) machines is critical for minimizing downtime and maximizing productivity. This paper presents a novel framework that integrates artificial intelligence (AI) with digital twin technology for predictive maintenance in CNC operations. By leveraging IoT (Internet of Things) sensors, real-time data is collected from CNC machines, enabling the creation of a dynamic digital twin that accurately represents machine performance and behavior. Hereby, employing advanced machine learning techniques, specifically XGBoost, to analyze historical and real-time data, facilitating the early detection of potential failures and optimizing maintenance schedules. It not only enhances the accuracy of maintenance predictions but also significantly reduces the maintenance cost and unplanned machine downtimes. This research contributes to the ongoing development of smart manufacturing systems and underscores the importance of AI-driven solutions in enhancing predictive maintenance strategies within the industrial sector.

title: Sok: Zero Trust as a Strategy to Address Devsecops Challenges
authors: A. Nair; S. Nicolazzo; A. Nocera; R. R. K. A.; V. P.
abstract: Over recent years, Development, Security, and Operations (DevSecOps, hereafter) has evolved as a unique shift-left strategy that integrates security practices, early on in the Development and Operations (DevOps, for short) software development methodology. However, DevSecOps is not devoid of challenges. Insecure tools and insider attacks are some of the threats that can escape the security controls enforced in DevSecOps pipelines. In this paper, we analyze the possibility of embedding Zero Trust into the organization's developer workflow as a strategy to further secure DevSecOps by removing the implicit trust among the various components of the pipelines. Based on a systematic review of the present literature and for each phase of the DevSecOps life cycle, we evaluated the possible integration of current ZTA approaches.

title: Enhancing Interoperability and system performance through Automation and testing of IoT sensors
authors: R. J; A. P. Patil; R. Sankarasubramanian; S. P. Yelaka; M. J; K. B. C. R
abstract: Seamless interoperability and enhanced system performance for real-time monitoring and efficient operation in smart environments are achieved through improved IoT sensor integration and automated testing and validation of backend APIs. By automating the processes of sensor data collection and API validation, the proposed method improves system efficiency, accuracy, and scalability within IoT environments. The central goal is to design a unified platform simplifying sensor deployment and ensuring consistent, reliable communication with backend systems. The proposed solution introduces a middleware layer that facilitates IoT sensor integration by unifying data formats and communication standards. It includes a backend API testing framework, leveraging tools like Cypress to verify API responses for accuracy, performance, and error resilience. Key components of this system include real-time simulation of sensor data, automated generation of test cases, and seamless integration with CI/CD pipelines for ongoing validation. Technologies such as Node.js, Python, and RESTful APIs are used to maintain scalability and system compatibility.The developed system offers a streamlined and automated approach to managing IoT sensors and verifying API interactions. Users can set up sensors, simulate their output, and validate backend responses without manual input. This level of automation reduces the time required for deployment, decreases the likelihood of errors, and ensures consistent performance of backend services. The proposed methodology demonstrates significant improvements in the efficiency and dependability of IoT-based systems.

title: A Comprehensive Review on Scaling Machine Learning Workflows Using Cloud Technologies and DevOps
authors: G. Ramesh; T. V. Pai; R. Birau; K. K. Poojary; Abhay; A. R. Shingad; N. Sowjanya; V. Popescu; A. T. Mitroi; R. M. Nioata Chireac; K. M. K. Raj
abstract: Scaling Machine Learning (ML) workflows in cloud environments presents critical challenges in ensuring reproducibility, low-latency inference, infrastructure reliability, and regulatory compliance. This review addresses the lack of a comprehensive synthesis of how integrated DevOps practices and cloud-native technologies enable scalable, production-grade ML systems. We analyze the convergence of MLOps with tools such as Kubernetes, Jenkins, and Terraform, detailing their role in automating CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure provisioning, and model lifecycle management. The main highlights strategies for optimizing resource utilization, minimizing inference latency, and managing data versioning across hybrid and multi-cloud architectures (AWS, Azure, GCP). We also examine serverless computing, container orchestration, and monitoring practices to enhance scalability and governance. By categorizing challenges chronologically and evaluating emerging practices such as federated learning and security-by-design, this work bridges a key gap in existing literature. It offers a unified perspective on building reliable, reproducible, and compliant ML workflows, thereby advancing the state of scalable AI system engineering.

title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Context-Aware Modeling Protocols for Improved Patient-Centric Healthcare Systems
authors: M. Meshram; A. J. Rangari; S. Madhukar Nagrare
abstract: The given paper proposes an innovative approach embedding the concept of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with that of context-aware modeling protocols as a means of facilitating patient-centric healthcare systems. The approach involves machine learning such as deep and reinforcement learning, augmented by real-time context data provided by IoMT sensors to perform intelligent, dynamically customized patient care. The framework enables predictive diagnostics, uninterrupted monitoring, and responsive treatment planning by adjusting healthcare responses to the context of specific patient based on factors such as physiological, environmental, and behavioral factors. Main research findings show that it achieved significant advances in accuracy, soundness and reaction times regarding conventional methods. Integrated system has a great potential of minimizing the number of clinical errors, enhancing good judgment, and eventually delivering smarter real time care to patients. Testings with artificial and actual health data sets validate the possibility of the system to stimulate compelling intelligent and patient-centered healthcare services.

title: Advanced Securing Cloud Environments using Quantum Convolutional Neural Network-based Multi-Channel Cryptographic
authors: K. K. T. M; C. Mavani; H. Mistry; C. Thacker; R. M. Shirish; M.SivaramKrishnan
abstract: The rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has led to an unprecedented aggregation of sensitive information within cloud infrastructures, consequently accentuating vulnerabilities associated with confidentiality, data integrity, and infrastructural resilience. Furthermore, extant privacy frameworks not only face imminent threat from forthcoming quantum decryption capabilities but also exhibit inherent weaknesses attributable to centralized data architectures. In order to confront this intricate and evolving risk landscape, we present a multi-layered security architecture that integrates heuristic anomaly detection, countermeasures against inference-based and anomaly attacks, post-quantum encryption, and a distributed ledger architecture—thereby establishing a coherent and uniform defensive paradigm. Suspicious transaction detection at the initial screening stage relies upon the identification of multi-canonical anomalous transactions, applied through a Multi-Channel Quantum Convolution Neural Network. This core mechanism is synergistically enhanced by a Walk-Spread search algorithm, which prioritises the identification of anomalous transaction patterns across temporal scales mediated by quantum temporal frameworks, effectively strengthening detection capabilities. Recorded transaction payloads within the proposed system are secured through the McEliece post-quantum encryption scheme, thereby constructing a formidable cryptographic bulwark against a wide array of adversarial efforts, including those mounted by both classical and quantum computational means. Building upon this foundation, a streamlined adaptation of Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) is engineered, realising a declarative and resource-efficient blockchain architecture that retains key attributes of consensus, immutability, cryptographic tamper-resistance, and thoroughly decentralised ledger operation while maintaining a and of very modest persistent computational cost. Evaluation against realistically emulative workload parameters demonstrates an anomaly detection accuracy exceeding 99%, with both precision and F1-score metrics achieving consensus at the operational maximum, collectively corroborating the system's resilience and effective adherence to operational metrics across contend time horizon.
keywords: Cloud Computing;Security;Multi-Channel Quantum Convolutional Neural Network;McEliece Post-Quantum Cryptosystem;Walk-Spread Algorithm

title: Cybersecurity in DevOps Environments: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: R. Carlos Bautista Ramos; S. G. Yoo
abstract: This systematic literature review provides a comprehensive analysis of the most critical cybersecurity challenges in DevOps environments. Through a rigorous examination of 62 peer-reviewed articles published between 2016 and 2025, we identified recurring threats, active attack vectors, structural vulnerabilities, mitigation strategies, and their technical impact on system performance and operational resilience. The analysis revealed that the most significant threats are related to uncontrolled automation, exposure of sensitive secrets in CI/CD pipelines, lack of mutual authentication between distributed services, supply chain attacks, and the use of unauthorized tools (Shadow IT). These threats simultaneously compromise core security principles, including integrity, confidentiality, and traceability. The most frequent attack vectors include code injection in CI/CD pipelines, unrestricted access to public repositories, remote execution via default configurations, and lateral movement in flat architectures. We identified 27 recurrent vulnerabilities throughout the DevOps lifecycle. The most critical include the absence of automated security testing, poor management of secrets, and reliance on unverified third-party components. More than 30 technical and organizational countermeasures were documented, such as SAST/DAST/IAST scans, infrastructure-as-code validation, secure credential storage via vaults, and integrated practices like DevSecOps and compliance-as-code. When properly implemented, these strategies do not degrade system performance and may even enhance resilience and stability. Nonetheless, a lack of comparative empirical validation in most reviewed studies limits the generalizability of proposed solutions. These findings establish a foundation for future research in emerging domains, such as the Internet of Things, where continuous, adaptive, and verifiable security is paramount for automated and dynamic environments.

title: Telcoformrix: An AI-Augmented Framework for Declarative and Scalable Provisioning of Real-Time Communication Infrastructure (Work in Progress)
authors: S. K. Davuluri; V. Challagulla; V. Mudapaka; U. Konka
abstract: The growing demand for real-time communication (RTC) services necessitates more efficient and reliable infrastructure provisioning methods. This work-inprogress paper introduces Telcoformrix, an AI-native Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) framework designed to simplify the deployment of RTC infrastructure. By leveraging a fine-tuned large language model (LLM), Telcoformrix translates high-level YAML declarations into Terraform JSON configurations, abstracting the complexities of cloud and edge network setup. Integrated with GitOps workflows, the framework aims to automate validation and deployment via CI/CD pipelines. This paper outlines the motivation, design, and planned evaluation of Telcoformrix, positioning it as a promising approach to reducing cognitive load and configuration errors in RTC infrastructure management.

title: Applying Monolithic to Microservices Strategy for Elastic Container Deployment for AI Applications
authors: A. H. P. A; A. O; B. A. Jose; A. Harikrishnan; K. Elengickal
abstract: As applications adopt Artificial Intelligence (AI), cloud deployment of AI models becomes a challenge due to size, cost and latency. This paper presents a study on adopting a monolithic AI application to a microservices-based AI architecture for cloud. The study involves containerizing services using Docker, deploying them via AWS ECS with both Fargate and EC2 backends and evaluating the performance of the application based on latency and cost. Experimental results demonstrate that, while serverless containers via Fargate offer cost benefits and ease of deployment, GPU-intensive services significantly benefit from ECS with EC2 instances. The microservices approach, combined with strategic deployment choices, improves scalability, maintainability, and system reliability for AI workloads in cloud-native environments.

title: Cloud-Native Hybrid Deployment Technology Under Narrowband Communication Conditions
authors: L. Wang; Z. Yang; C. Zhong; W. Zhang
abstract: Edge computing extends cloud capabilities to the network periphery to reduce latency and bandwidth usage, but implementing cloud-native technologies in these environments poses unique challenges. This paper surveys cloud-native hybrid deployment strategies under narrowband communication conditions, as encountered in IoT and remote edge scenarios. We review the state of the art in general-purpose edge computing, focusing on containerization and orchestration frameworks that bridge cloud and edge deployments despite constrained network bandwidth. Key platforms and tools are examined in depth, including Kubernetes for container orchestration, lightweight Kubernetes variants like K3s and edge-specific frameworks like KubeEdge, package management with Helm, GitOps continuous delivery via Argo CD, event-driven scaling with KEDA, and the integration of security through DevSecOps practices. We describe architectural approaches for hybrid cloud-edge orchestration, evaluate each solution's design, and discuss how they accommodate intermittent connectivity and low data rates. Through careful analysis of existing literature and industry practices, we highlight how cloud-native paradigms can be adapted to bandwidth-constrained edge environments, identify open challenges in managing deployments over narrowband links, and outline future research directions in optimizing cloud-edge synergy under network limitations.

title: Secure Deployment of 5G/B5G Core Network
authors: A. Landa-Arrue; M. Barceló; I. Garitano; A. Urbieta
abstract: The deployment of secure and resilient FithGeneration (5G) core networks in industrial environments necessitates adopting methodologies that integrate security seamlessly into the entire development lifecycle. This paper presents a Development, Security, and Operations-based (DevSecOps) Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline designed to enhance the security of distributed 5G core networks. The proposed pipeline systematically analyzes Docker images and Kubernetes templates, detecting and mitigating vulnerabilities early in the deployment process. Automated tools such as Trivy, Checkov, Kubelinter, and Kube-bench are employed to significantly reduce security risks associated with outdated dependencies, misconfigurations, and network vulnerabilities. Additionally, integrating Lamassu IoT, a specialized PKI, enables automated digital certificate management. Results demonstrate substantial improvements in security practices, showing a marked reduction in vulnerabilities and enhanced compliance with industry standards.

title: DevDocOps: Automated Documentation in DevOps Through Infrastructure as Code Using the CALMS Framework
authors: A. Ali; M. A. Zia; F. Mehmood; M. A. Nawaz; A. Basit; M. A. Naeem
abstract: Integrating DevOps into software development has transformed workflows by emphasizing automation and seamless communication. However, challenges in software documentation, such as ensuring security, integrity, dependability, and timely delivery, continue to hinder development and support processes. To address these problems, an innovative approach called DevDocOps has emerged, boosting the software documentation process and accelerating development activities. This research highlights DevDocOps as an enhancement of DevOps, leveraging automation to improve documentation accuracy and decrease delivery time while bridging the gap between customers and support teams. A key component of this study is implementing the iDoc tool, which mechanizes software documentation, improves process reliability, and reduces the time required for documentation tasks. The procedure centers on approving the CALMS (Culture, Automation, Lean, Measurement, and Sharing) framework, prioritizing efficient service delivery, client procedures, and an ethos of rapid reaction loops. The study also unites DevSecOps principles to support security throughout the software development lifecycle to integrate Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices, encouraged by Google’s approach to merging software engineering with IT operations. By joining these methodologies, the suggested approach delivers a robust, adjustable, and secure documentation process that aligns with modern DevOps prototypes. Results determine that adopting DevDocOps expressively improves the productivity and consistency of software documentation, decreases manual effort, and confirms alignment with future technological changes.

title: Leveraging AI and MLOps for IoT-Edge-Cloud Industrial Digital Twins: a Practical Case Study
authors: M. A. Farooq; P. Bellavista; A. Bujari; A. Sita
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) are crucial for the practical application of Digital Twins (DT) in industrial environments. DT facilitate enhanced modelling, forecasting, and optimisation of assets and processes, while MLOps ensure resilient, reliable, and continuously updated models. This paper proposes an industrial-grade DT example for the manufacturing industry, utilising cloud/edge-based AI technologies from the Microsoft Azure ecosystem. Data handling and ML model training are performed at the cloud layer, while models are deployed and maintained at the edge. To enhance interoperability and portability, trained ML models are converted into lightweight and portable models using the Open Neural Network Exchange format (ONNX) standard. Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) are performed on an industrial edge device using GitHub Actions. REST APIs are implemented using standard HTTP methods to manage the IoT Central edge manifest. In-the-field experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our DT prototype in a specific industrial use case.

title: AI-Driven Predictive Patient Monitoring System Using Kubeflow and CI/CD Enabled MLOps Framework
authors: D. Sundaram
abstract: Continuous and intelligent patient monitoring is essential for improving clinical outcomes and preventing avoidable deterioration in hospitals and remote care environments. Traditional systems rely on static thresholds and manual review, often missing subtle changes in patient status and contributing to alarm fatigue. This paper presents an AI-driven predictive monitoring system that integrates real-time physiological data streams with a Kubeflow-based MLOps pipeline and a fully automated CI/CD workflow. The system continuously learns from patient-specific baselines and adapts to evolving clinical patterns through automated retraining, validation, and deployment. By combining personalized risk modeling, scalable cloud-native architecture, and explainable AI, the proposed solution enhances early-warning capabilities and supports timely decision-making across ICU, chronic-care, and remote-monitoring scenarios.

title: Design and Comparison of Enhanced P&O and FOCV-Based MPPT for Indoor Light Energy Harvesting in 65 NM CMOS Process
authors: R. M. Sabarillo; Q. P. S. Patulin; L. M. M. Mamburao; W. K. V. Pitogo
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of two maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms-Enhanced Perturb and Observe (P&O) and Fractional Open-Circuit Voltage (FOCV)-targeted for indoor photovoltaic (PV) energy harvesting applications. Both designs were implemented using the 65 nm CMOS process in Cadence Virtuoso and integrated with a boost converter to ensure efficient energy transfer under low-light conditions. The evaluation focuses on key performance metrics including output voltage, settling time, ripple voltage, boost accuracy, and power consumption. Simulation results show that both algorithms achieve comparable performance in terms of output voltage stability and ripple control, with post-simulation ripple voltages of 0.622 % for Enhanced $\mathrm{P} \& \mathrm{O}$ and 0.641 % for FOCV, and boost accuracies above 99 % for both. However, Enhanced P&O clearly outperforms FOCV in terms of settling time, achieving $370 \mu ~\mathrm{s}$ compared to $810 \mu ~\mathrm{s}$, making it more suitable for applications requiring dynamic adaptation and fasttracking response. On the other hand, while FOCV demonstrates slightly higher power consumption and slower response, it offers lower circuit complexity and simplified control implementation due to the absence of current sensing and a feedback loop. These trade-offs highlight the strengths of each technique depending on application-specific constraints.
keywords: MPPT;energy harvesting systems;fractional open-circuit voltage;perturb and observe;PV cells

title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to DevOps: A Study on AI-Driven Anomaly Detection and Predictive Maintenance in Cloud Environments
authors: A. Patel; R. Laudya; H. Ragothaman; P. Pandey
abstract: This research focuses on adopting AI as an innovative technology in the DevOps framework for detecting anomalies and implementing predictive maintenance in compute clouds. The use of DevOps in cloud computing has become popular due to the new complexities that need to be effectively dealt with by prior forms of DevOps. AI’s automated way can detect anomalies, explore the possibility of System Failure, and prevent them from happening with the help of such technology. This research aims to analyze the main options for enhancing DevOps employing AI and consider the effectiveness of AI solutions in cloud environments. In some areas, such as anomaly detection and predictive maintenance, ensuring the key aims are defined and quantifiable in the evaluation metric data will be essential. The major measures are accuracy, the measure of precision, and the measure of recall and F1 measure.

title: Continuous Integration for Electronic Products–Enabled by Digital Twins
authors: C. Wolff; P. Schulz; J. Rettkowski; N. Sleibi; S. Trimech; C. Hensen
abstract: The need for frequent new features, bug fixes and updates has led to the development of the continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) paradigm in software production. For embedded systems, this transformation is inhibited mainly by the constraints of electronics manufacturing, both in prototyping and in production and delivery of the final product. Nevertheless, the agile transformation of the embedded systems market requires a more flexible and continuous integration of new features while the growing complexity leads to more frequent bug fixes. The main inhibiting factor is the high effort and turn-around time (TAT) for changes of the hardware of the product or the production systems. This contribution presents the concept of a CI engineering chain and design flow for electronic products based on the adaptation of the concept of the digital twin. This concept connects the model-based systems engineering (MBSE) approaches used in the frontend of the engineering chain (development, verification) with the established concept of the digital twin in the backend of the chain (production, product test, logistics, deployment) by enhancing the structural system descriptions contained in “classical” digital twins with the functional models used in MBSE. The concept is illustrated by mapping it to the case of an electronics manufacturing service (EMS) provider.

title: Security-Integrated DevOps Pipeline System with Context-Aware Hybrid Stimulation Engine for Continuous Software Assurance
authors: S. Kurapati; V. R; A. K. Bhardwaj; S. R K; P. Anugula
abstract: Recently, DevOps pipelines have allowed continuous delivery, but treat security as a late-stage checklist by leaving a blind spot for stealthy supply chains that are activated only in specific environments. However, the existing dynamic analysis fails to detect stealthy malicious behaviors. Hence, this study proposes a Context-Aware Hybrid Stimulation Engine (CAHSE) to address this issue by creating realistic conditions that trick hidden malicious code into execution. Initially, the static probe extracts seeds and hotspots using Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)-based scanning and produces a stimulation plan for targeted testing. Then, an environment emulation and sandbox setup recreate realistic external contexts through a per-package Docker sandbox; thus, environmentgated logic runs. Subsequently, guided fuzzing with lightweight concolic exploration synthesizes realistic parameters to unlock the hidden branches and produce execution traces. Furthermore, Reinforcement Learning (RL)-based steering prioritizes promising environmental strategies to focus on computing high-yield tests and provides a shortlist of suspicious runs. Finally, behavioral differential analysis and heuristic rule matching compare the baseline and stimulated runs to generate an explainable detection report. The proposed CAHSE achieved better results than the existing Open-Source Software Supply Chain Attack Robust Detection (OSCAR) in terms of recall $\boldsymbol{(} 0.93$) and $\mathbf{F 1}$-score (0.92) respectively.

title: Dynamic Integration and Full-Process Automation of Agile R&D Toolchain for Software Factories
authors: L. Zheng; X. Xie; B. Hou; D. Zhang
abstract: As software development methodologies evolve toward Agile and DevOps practices, the demands for automation and efficient collaboration in product development and delivery processes have become increasingly stringent. Traditional R&D toolchains suffer from insufficient integration and severe data silos, which constrain delivery efficiency and quality control in software factories. Against the backdrop of enterprise digital transformation, this paper designs and implements a research and development toolchain integration solution tailored to actual software development scenarios, covering product automated delivery, automated testing, and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD). Through interface integration, RPA-based automated operations, containerized deployment, and digital model-driven approaches, the solution enables end-to-end connectivity of development data, automated generation of deliverables, closed-loop regression testing, and full-process automation of CI/CD pipelines. Practical applications demonstrate that this solution significantly improves delivery efficiency, traceability of quality issues, and observability of development processes, verifying the engineering application value of R&D toolchain integration.

title: A Blockchain Integrated DevSecOps Framework for Secure and Transparent Pipelines
authors: J. J; H. S; N. N
abstract: DevSecOps pipelines are increasingly adopted to automate software integration, testing, security analysis, and deployment. However, centralized mechanisms for access control and logging remain vulnerable to unauthorized access, log tampering, and insider threats. To address these issues, this work proposes a blockchain-enabled DevSecOps framework that enhances security, transparency, and auditability. Smart contracts implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), ensuring that sensitive operations such as deployments or access to critical security data are performed only by authorized users. Security events, vulnerability reports, and deployment records are immutably stored on the blockchain, creating a verifiable and tamper-resistant audit trail. The framework integrates standard DevSecOps practices with a decentralized trust layer to reduce risks of manipulation and compliance failures. By combining blockchain with CI/CD automation, security scanning, and monitoring, the proposed system strengthens resilience against cyber threats and insider risks while providing a scalable, trustworthy approach for securing modern software delivery pipelines.
keywords: DevSecOps;Blockchain;Smart Contract;Role-based access control;Continuous Integration and Deployment

title: Architecting Observability for AI-Driven Microservices at Scale
authors: M. K. Gaddam
abstract: The increasing adoption of AI-driven microservices in large-scale distributed systems has amplified the complexity of system monitoring, performance tuning, and failure resolution. This paper presents a scalable observability architecture tailored specifically for AI-driven microservices, addressing the inherent opacity and dynamism of AI workloads. By integrating fine-grained telemetry, trace correlation, anomaly detection, and model-centric metrics, the proposed framework enables enhanced visibility across the entire AI pipeline—from data ingestion to model inference. Our approach demonstrates improved root cause analysis, reduced system downtime, and increased transparency in model performance behavior. The architecture is validated through a real-world deployment on a Kubernetes-based AI platform, showing minimal performance overhead while maintaining high fidelity in observability signals. This work contributes a blueprint for building resilient, transparent, and scalable AI-driven systems, critical for operations in production environments.

title: Edge-Cloud Architectures for Distributed, Real-Time Systems in Mission-Critical Domains
authors: S. Telalwar
abstract: Real-time systems deployed in mission-critical domains such as autonomous transportation, industrial control, and emergency response demand stringent latency, availability, and fault tolerance guarantees. Traditional cloud-centric solutions, while scalable, suffer from high latency and centralized failure risks, whereas isolated edge deployments lack global context and resilience. Despite substantial advances in distributed architectures, a consistent and unified approach balancing edge-cloud orchestration for real-time responsiveness remains a pressing gap. This paper introduces a novel edge-cloud architectural framework that leverages event-driven microservices and real-time stream processing across a multi-tier deployment. Our architecture integrates resilient fault-containment algorithms, DevSecOps pipelines, and a latency-aware scheduling model tailored to deterministic deadlines. Extensive evaluation demonstrates an average 37.2% reduction in response latency under load, a 29.5% faster recovery time after simulated failures, and a 46.8% improvement in availability compared to leading monolithic cloud deployments. These results substantiate the viability of our framework in time-sensitive, failure-intolerant scenarios. The proposed solution offers a modular foundation for future intelligent systems operating in edge-cloud environments.

title: An Open-Source Approach for Emulating Complex Embedded Systems: Enhancing Software Verification with Radiation-Induced Fault Injection
authors: M. De Clercq
abstract: The growing complexity of embedded systems in safety-critical domains such as automotive, aerospace, and New Space demands verification methods that are both comprehensive and scalable. Traditional hardware-based testing, while indispensable for final certification, is time-consuming and costly to adapt for early-stage development and continuous integration pipelines. This paper introduces a novel open-source approach that integrates two powerful emulation platforms, Renode and QEMU, for software-centric correctness testing. The proposed approach supports complex multi-node configurations, enabling the emulation of both low-power microcontrollers and high-performance systems-on-chip (SoCs). A key feature is the ability to perform advanced fault injection — including simulation of radiation-induced SEUs and transient faults — which are notoriously difficult to replicate on physical hardware. We present a proof-of-concept case study featuring an emulated Raspberry Pi Pico (Cortex-M0+) and a Linux-class ARM SoC node (QEMU AArch64 virt, approximating a Raspberry Pi 5–class system) communicating through CAN and UART. Experimental results show that our proposed approach provides broad fault coverage, flexible integration into CI/CD pipelines, and a reduction in testing overhead compared to traditional methods in our experiments.

title: Identifying and Architecting Microservices for Edge Computing
authors: U. Vora
abstract: Microservices architecture (MSA) paradigm extends Service Oriented Architecture (SOA) to focus on specific aspects such as design of small lightweight services as independent cohesive components, development and service management using agile and DevOps methodologies and service delivery based on distributed data management and decentralized service governance and more. MSA thus has become a widely used architectural style for designing modern applications due to advantages like granular scalability and maintainability, especially in today's world of ‘system of systems’. Edge computing facilitates segregation of computing responsibilities between edge devices and cloud infrastructure to process and analyze data acquired by edge devices. The number of IoT devices is increasing at such a high rate that the need for Edge AI is expected to reach the value of investment to USD 72.6 billion by 2030. The edge analytics bring correlated research challenges from the areas of cyber and physical security, data privacy, maintenance support, access, latency, reliability, power consumption and remoteness into the scope and require innovation at architecture level as does the improvement in all systems' quality related attributes. In this tutorial we discuss how microservices paradigm can be used effectively for edge computing-based systems resulting in a sustainable architecture with lower dependency on the data-center / cloud architecture.

title: MLCAE: A Multi-Layered Configuration for Architectural Elements in Large-Scale Software Applications
authors: H. Hristov
abstract: The increasing complexity of large-scale software applications, such as ERP, CRM and DMS, requires advanced approaches for organizing and managing architectural elements (AEs) including architectures, architectural patterns, technologies, frameworks, standards, methodologies, etc. This paper introduces MLCAE (Multi-Layered Configuration for Architectural Elements), a novel model for architectural modeling that provides a structured, flexible and scalable way of positioning AEs across multiple layers. MLCAE defines a set of standard layers (Core, Communication, Deployment) and allows for the dynamic creation of non-standard layers (Security, Monitoring, DevOps pipelines, Integration, etc.), depending on project-specific requirements. The model supports role-based placement of AEs (Primary Layer Placement, Secondary Layer Presence, Interface Anchors, Deployment Bindings), indexing mechanisms for managing overlapping AEs across multiple systems and categorization to differentiate between architectural types. Furthermore, MLCAE introduces layer priorities for conflict resolution and architectural packages to group cross-layer AEs. A case study with ERP, CRM, DMS, PLM and SCM demonstrates the practical applicability of MLCAE in enterprise environments, showing improvements in coverage, conflict resolution and integration compared to traditional architectural modeling. The results indicate that MLCAE can serve as a strategic tool for enterprise architecture management and future research directions include AI-assisted classification of AEs and automated visualization dashboards.

title: Deployment and Design of AI-Powered Edge Systems for Wildlife Monitoring: A Survey
authors: M. Martinský; J. Papán; S. Tatarka
abstract: Wildlife monitoring increasingly employs artificial intelligence (AI) for automated detection, classification, and tracking in natural habitats. While cloud-based approaches provide strong computational resources, they face latency, connectivity, and energy limitations in remote areas. Edge computing addresses these constraints by enabling local inference on distributed devices, reducing bandwidth demand and supporting real-time analytics. This survey reviews deployment and design strategies for AI-powered edge systems in wildlife monitoring, with focus on standalone, edge–cloud and federated architectures. We further examine containerization, orchestration frameworks, and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) practices in distributed environments. Specific attention is given to device heterogeneity, energy management, and long-term reliability under field conditions. Finally, we outline open challenges and research directions toward scalable, sustainable and autonomous wildlife monitoring with edge AI.

title: On-Demand Cardiac Digital Twins: A Case Study on DevOps workflows for Digital Twin Platforms
authors: P. Yelkotwar; R. Raj; A. Pingle; P. Talasila; N. Goveas
abstract: Digital Twins (DTs), when integrated with physical systems and their virtual representations, can support real-time analysis, simulations, and decision-making. A major barrier to creating DTs is the effort required to put together the techniques and technologies developed by subject experts. The Digital Twin as a Service (DTaaS) is a DT platform that helps in DT development by creating collaborative environments in which users can develop, use, and share DTs. While experts can create and customize DTs to their needs, non-expert users benefit from automated solutions for on-demand deployment and execution of DTs. Modern software engineering practices such as Development and Operations (DevOps) have produced architectural solutions for a scalable deployment of software products. In this work, we present our contribution to the integration of DevOps workflows with the DTaaS platform. We develop a cardiac DT for ECGbased preventive diagnostics of the human heart. The same DT is used to demonstrate an implementation of DevOps workflows on the DTaaS platform. We find that our proposed solution is suitable for time-sensitive applications and flexible enough to be used with other DT platforms.

title: Model Drift Detection and Automated Retraining in Production ML System
authors: V. Srinivasan; J. R; A. R; Chethan
abstract: This paper presents DRIFT-ACT (Drift-Aware Continuous Training), a practical and modular framework designed to tackle the persistent challenge of model performance degradation in real-world AI systems. DRIFT-ACT combines real-time drift detection using lightweight statistical monitoring techniques with automated retraining pipelines powered by MLOps tools. Instead of modifying the core model architecture, DRIFT-ACT operates as a thin, flexible layer on top of existing systems monitoring, detecting, and adapting to shifts in data or concept distributions without human intervention. Tested across synthetic and real-world production scenarios, DRIFT-ACT significantly improves model robustness over time, reduces manual maintenance effort, and ensures sustained performance consistency. Beyond the technical solution, this work serves as a practical blueprint for deploying resilient ML systems in dynamic, high-impact environments.

title: Beyond Container CVE Analysis: A GitOps-Based Attestation and Sandbox Framework for Container Supply Chains
authors: E. Syrmos; P. Radoglou-Grammatikis; E. Katsaros; J. S. Banerjee; A. Kazakli; K. Panitsidis; V. Vitsas; P. Sarigiannidis
abstract: As software supply chain accelerate through DevOps automation and continuous delivery, container images have become the primary vector for both application development and security compromise. While static vulnerability scanners can detect known CVEs, they are unable to uncover zero-day malware or runtime threats- particularly in container images sourced from public registries, which are maintained by individual contributors of varying intent and trustworthiness. In this paper, we introduce a GitOps-drive sandboxing framework for proactive and tamper-resistant container image attestation, addressing the urgent need for deeper analysis before deployment. Our approach combines static vulnerability detection with dynamic behavioral inspection using gVisor-based sandboxing. Through filesystem analysis, system call tracing, and network activity monitoring, the framework identifies malicious patterns and anomalies. Adopting this framework will empower developers and security teams to enforce stronger trust guarantees even in the absence of SBOMs or SLSA levels. This framework lays the foundations for a resilient, trustworthy software delivery at scale in compliance with NIST SP 800-218 and ISO/IEC 27001 standards.

title: Impedance Matching Technique for Dual-Band Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting Unit utilizing 900MHz (UHF) and 2.45GHz (Wi-Fi) Frequency Band
authors: M. A. T. S. Teleron; A. M. M. Vergara; F. X. Zhu; J. A. Hora
abstract: This study presents a dual-band impedance matching technique designed for wireless power transfer (WPT) applications operating at 900 MHz (UHF/GSM) and 2.45 GHz (Wi-Fi/ISM) frequencies. The proposed method employs a bridged-T coil (BTC) network integrated with a single-stub tuning approach to simultaneously match the input impedance at both frequency bands, ensuring efficient power delivery. Fabricated using 65nm CMOS technology, the rectifier circuit demonstrates promising performance metrics. At an input power of −15dBm, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) reaches 58.01 percent at 900 MHz and 50.52 percent at 2.45 GHz. Under higher input power of −3 dBm, the peak PCE improves to 68.57 and 57.44 percent for 900 MHz and 2.45 GHz, respectively. The design also achieves a dynamic range of 19.04 dB at 2.45 GHz, indicating robust performance across varying input levels. Furthermore, excellent return loss (S11) values are observed, with −34.48 dB and −13.27 dB at 900 MHz, and −11.28 dB and −16.27 dB at 2.45 GHz for GSM and Wi-Fi bands, respectively.
keywords: Energy Harvesting;Dual Band;Bridged T-Coil (BTC);Radio Frequency (RF);Impedance Matching Network (IMN)

title: Streamlining Kubernetes Deployments through GitOps Methodologies
authors: S. Kurrewar; S. Dhomane; A. Dahake; R. K. Yadav; N. Wyawahare; N. C. Morris
abstract: A clear process for automating the deployment of apps on Kubernetes using GitOps concepts is shown, with an emphasis on tools like Helm and Argo CD. The method demonstrates how to improve the effectiveness and reliability of application delivery by utilizing techniques like infrastructure- as-code, YAML configuration files, and CI/CD pipelines through GitHub Actions. The entities can accomplish reliable and repeatable deployments while developing teamwork among development teams by considering Git as the primary source of information. Applications remain in their original state with the support of Argo CD's continuous delivery, and monitoring tools provide data that is insightful on resource use and performance. By optimizing the management of cloud-native apps, our research helps people remain effective in the face of rapidly evolving technology. All things considered, the results demonstrate how applying GitOps techniques can streamline deployment procedures and improve application management in Kubernetes systems.

title: The Science of Threat Modeling in Complex Industrial Systems
authors: S. Singh; P. Desai; S. Amilkanthwar
abstract: As modern computing environments evolve into intricate, distributed ecosystems that span native cloud architectures, microservices, IoT networks, and multi-cloud infrastructures, the need for robust, scalable, and adaptive threat modeling has never been more urgent. Traditional methodologies such as STRIDE and PASTA, while foundational, fall short in addressing the dynamic nature, scale, and interdependencies of complex systems. This paper dives into a comprehensive analysis of the limitations of classical approaches and highlights emerging advances designed to meet contemporary security challenges that are immediately applicable to complex systems that are typical in the industry. We synthesize the recent literature across multiple domains to evaluate adaptive methodologies that incorporate automation, graph based modeling, DevSecOps pipeline integration, infrastructure-as-code (IaC) scanning, and AI assisted threat analysis. The paper also introduces a comparative framework to assess traditional and modern techniques across representative system architectures, including IoT, microservices, and native cloud deployments. We identify open research challenges, such as continuous threat modeling, collaborative usability, and integration of run time telemetry, and offer actionable recommendations for building context aware, scalable, and living threat models. By uniting classical rigor with modern agility, this work aims to guide industry practitioners and researchers toward the next generation of threat modeling solutions for complex and rapidly evolving environments.

title: GATEKEEPER Platform: Secure Processing Environment for European Health Data Space
authors: E. Gaeta; M. Salman Haleem; L. Lopez-Perez; M. Manea; M. Fernanda Cabrera Umpierrez; M. Teresa Arredondo Waldmeyer; L. Pecchia; G. Fico
abstract: The European Health Data Space (EHDS) is a significant initiative within the European Union aimed at improving healthcare through better use of health data and collaboration. This involves sharing and utilization of health data in a secure and interoperable manner across EU member states. With the advent of modern technology, different types of health data are being acquired ranging from traditional electronic health records to real-time wearable signals for improved healthcare delivery and management. However, there are certain challenges associated with compliance to EHDS, such as secure continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD), scalability and adaptability towards new technologies and applications, tolerance against IoT cyber-attacks, requirement of advanced data storage methods, processing power, interoperability solutions for data analysis and connectivity. In order to address these, a flagship project of the European Commission, GATEKEEPER, represents a pioneering effort designed to transform healthcare delivery through the utilization of sophisticated digital technologies. The architecture of the GATEKEEPER platform has been meticulously crafted, in compliance with the EHDS, to integrate a multitude of data sources, deploying advanced analytical tools to enable the development of novel solutions for the effective prediction, detection, and management of chronic health conditions. GATEKEEPER addresses the aforementioned challenges by integrating collaborative tools for data management and consistency, machine learning modelling and management tool, activity feeds and issue tracking tools with developers authentication, CI/CD tools allowing, among others scalability in multiple formats, tools for assessing security, vulnerability and dependency for third party packages.
keywords: CI/CD;data scalability;data security;European health data space;healthcare platform;SecDevOps

title: Continuous Delivery Platform Development in the Cloud-Native Era
authors: Z. G. Yang; A. S. Alon; L. L. Alejandro; J. Paguigan; C. H. Benito
abstract: With the rapid development of cloud computing technologies and the widespread adoption of microservices architecture, traditional software development and deployment models can no longer meet the strict requirements of modern enterprises for rapid delivery, high availability, and security. This paper proposes and implements an enterprise-level cloud-native continuous delivery platform that adopts a Flask server-side rendering architecture and integrates core technological innovations including service-level fine-grained permission isolation, unified management of massive Kubernetes service configurations, and production environment stability enhancement. Through innovative production environment stability control mechanisms, the platform implements key functions such as core service mandatory waiting mechanisms, monitoring screenshot upload verification, release process pause/resume control, rapid rollback mechanisms, release time window control, automated security scanning, and release notification closed-loop management. Deeply integrated with mainstream CI/CD toolchains such as Jenkins, it supports end-to-end automated delivery from code commit to production, covering advanced deployment strategies such as canary releases and blue-green deployments. According to the evaluation strategy indicators, compared to the traditional "cloud-based virtual machines + Jenkins" model, the new platform has improved deployment efficiency, rollback time, resource utilization, and fault recovery capability by 85.7%, 85.5%, 52.1%, and 69.6% respectively, providing strong technical support for enterprise digital transformation and meeting ISO 25010 software quality standards and security compliance requirements for enterprise applications.

title: An Intelligent Hybrid Intrusion Detection and Prevention System for Threat Mitigation in High Bandwidth 5G/6G Network
authors: K. Mavale; A. Ingle; K. P. Kshirsagar; C. M. Reddy; P. D. Honawadajkar; V. M. Marathe
abstract: Fifth Generation (5G) and the impending Sixth Generation (6G) wireless communications revolutionize modern wireless communication with their record-breaking data speeds, low latency, and wide-ranging device connections. Standard Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems are ineffective in toxic security situations, which are brought on by current developments. In addition to anomaly-detection and signature-matching systems, this presents a new IDS and IPS system that leverages deep learning artificial intelligence to maximize high-speed network protection. The suggested approach is built on Software-Defined Networking, which enables dynamic security policy enforcement and quick threat responses. According to evaluation criteria of processing speed and detection accuracy with low false positive occurrence rates, the integrated solution performs optimally for securing next-generation mobile networks.

title: Industry Practice of LLM-Assisted Protocol Fuzzing for Commercial Communication Modules
authors: Q. Fu; C. Liu; Y. Ding; C. Fan; Y. Fu; Y. Chen; Y. Fu; R. Shi; F. Ma; H. Shi
abstract: Fuzzing is widely used for software robustness testing. However, its application in commercial communication modules remains limited due to several key challenges, including labor-intensive template generation, lack of coverage collection support, limited testing performance, and inconsistencies between practical hardware and software CI/CD processes. In collaboration with China Mobile IoT, we present FuzzCM, a comprehensive protocol fuzzing framework tailored for commercial communication modules. FuzzCM employs a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced large language model (LLM) to automate template generation and utilizes GPIO-based instrumentation for efficient runtime coverage data collection. Additionally, it leverages a knowledge base constructed from prior tests to guide hybrid mutation strategies and integrates CI/CD across both software and hardware layers, enabling continuous and environment-aware testing. We conducted an industrial practice with FuzzCM on five LTE Cat.1 bis modules, identifying 21 previously unknown bugs, 15 of which have been fixed. The results demonstrate that FuzzCM outperforms both manual methods and the Peach* approach, achieving average coverage improvements of 51% and 29%, respectively, with overall coverage reaching 85%.

title: Framework For Scalable Serverless Architecture Integrating Remote Sensing Image Classification
authors: A. Shrivastava; L. Hussein; V. Mittal; R. Kumar; S. Jain; M. K. Nigam
abstract: In the evolving landscape of web development, modern digital platforms demand scalability, agility, and seamless user experiences across devices. Traditional monolithic content management systems (CMS) often fall short in meeting these requirements due to their tightly coupled structures and limited flexibility. This paper proposes a scalable architecture that integrates serverless computing with headless CMS to decouple content delivery from backend logic. The architecture enables automatic scaling, faster deployment, improved performance, and cost efficiency. Through simulated experiments comparing four architectures—Monolithic CMS, Traditional CMS with Cloud, Headless CMS Only, and Serverless + Headless CMS—the study evaluates performance based on deployment time, scalability, operational cost, and page load time. Statistical analysis using ANOVA confirms that the serverless + headless CMS model consistently outperforms traditional approaches. Component-level analysis further demonstrates high reliability, maintainability, and cost-efficiency across key infrastructural layers. This architecture supports omnichannel content delivery, streamlines development workflows, and positions itself as a future-ready solution for building content-rich web applications.

title: AI-Driven Signal Processing: Improving Communication Systems with Machine Learning-Based Noise Reduction
authors: T. R. Singasani; M. S. Shaik; C. Gangajaliya; S. S. Ogety; V. A. B. Nallam; S. K. R. Katta
abstract: Signal processing plays an important role for transforming and analysing real-world signals like audio Important to process the signal efficiently and precisely. An AI approach to noise reduction using machine learning techniques are investigated in this work. We then use modern techniques such as Fourier Transform, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and de-noising autoencoders in order to remove noise while retaining important signal features. Method One proposed to employ machine learning models to adaptively eliminate the noise according to communication system, thus to improve the performance of communication systems. The experimental results suggest that using the artificial intelligence models to suppress the noise can suppress the noising efficiency and restore the signal nearly completely. These results illustrate the tremendous potential of AI as applied to signal processing in background noise. The AI models have also proved that, because they are trained to adapt to the kind of noise in the moment that it happens, they deliver a much better-quality signal than traditional methods. These characteristics are essential for the future communication systems which are required very high robustness and clearness.

title: AI Assisted Cloud Resources Allocation for Edge Computing
authors: S. K. Khanday
abstract: The growing adoption of edge-cloud computing has underscored the need for intelligent resource allocation frameworks capable of managing dynamic and heterogeneous workloads. This paper proposes a novel hybrid AI-driven framework that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformers to address the complexities of spatial and temporal data in edge-cloud environments. The framework leverages spatial-temporal attention mechanisms to capture critical workload patterns, cross-attention fusion to dynamically integrate spatial and temporal features, and adaptive filters to optimize resource allocation. Extensive experiments on a realworld edge computing dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of workload prediction accuracy, energy efficiency, and latency reduction. Specifically, the model achieves a 20.7% reduction in latency and an 18% improvement in energy efficiency compared to the best-performing baseline. Furthermore, scalability analysis highlights the robustness of the framework under increasing workloads, making it suitable for real-world deployment. This study contributes to the advancement of intelligent and adaptive resource management in edge-cloud computing systems, addressing key challenges such as heterogeneity, scalability, and real-time performance optimization.

title: MLCOps: a Platform to Support Cloud Continuum Machine Learning Operations
authors: A. Sabbioni; L. Serfilippi; S. Montebugnoli; A. Bujari; A. Corradi
abstract: The increasing reliance on Machine Learning (ML) to extract insights and value from data is driving researchers and businesses to seamlessly integrate it throughout the entire Cloud Continuum (CC), spanning from large-scale cloud infrastructures to edge computing and end devices. However, traditional service orchestration frameworks are fine-tuned to manage single-site general-purpose applications, struggling with the complexity of CC ML deployments, which seek customized strategies for enhanced performance and resiliency. To this end, we propose Machine Learning cloud Continuum Operations (MLCOps), an overlay solution that supports ML applications in CC deployments. MLCOps implements an innovative multisite orchestration layer and provides a new service runtime support, allowing one to react quickly to changing conditions. MLCOps advocates a layered approach to carry out specialized strategies, implementing global and local actions on infrastructure and environment to ensure the performance and availability of the deployed ML services. Without loss of generality, we show how the framework could be instantiated to support an anomaly detection task. In this context, we assess various (re)configuration strategies that can take place in actual deployments, assessing the ability of MLCOps to preserve the reliability of CC ML application deployments under dynamic workload conditions.

title: A Framework for Generative AI-Driven Application Modernization: Strategies and Case Studies
authors: A. Wairagade
abstract: The dynamism in technology makes it essential for organizations to update their old applications to newer ones. This paper explores how Generative AI (Gen AI) can transform the application modernization through automation of key tasks such as code refactoring, system refactoring and security integration. In the case of Gen AI, the applicability of various modern tools and methodologies such as cloud migration, microservices architecture, and automation frameworks, including DevOps, and emerging players in DevSecOps. This paper demonstrates how Gen AI as an organizational change supports continuous delivery, security integration, and operation resilience. In addition, the research examines cloud computing, microservices architecture, and DevOps for application modernization. It also addresses how Generative AI improves modernization enablers to optimize productivity, velocity, and project success. Through insights from case study, the work indicates GenAI produces 40-70 percent improvement in modernization cost, speed and accuracy. Finally, a structured framework is also proposed to help the organizations in adoption of GenAI for efficient and sustainable modernization.

title: Best Practices for Cloud, IT and Digital Infrastructure Programs Across Government Agencies
authors: J. A. Shah; N. Ramesh Iyer
abstract: Federal governments globally are evolving from a cloud-first policy to cloud-smart. This shift in approach allowed organizations to mature in their cloud journey, which increased the importance and need for the centralized IT cloud infrastructure program. A centralized cloud IT infrastructure program is a common operating model in federal public sector agencies and their service provides agencies and departments with crucial services in the broader cloud adoption and cloud operating journey. Serving agencies and departments as a technology partner is key from an infrastructure perspective, but there is a continued opportunity to serve as a business partner through the advisory lens. When measuring cloud IT infrastructure services, performance indicators and measures should be leveraged and monitored on an ongoing basis. The excellent or poor performance of a cloud IT infrastructure service directly impacts agencies and departments. Such cloud programs in the public sector position governments to be early adopters of innovations like AI, IoT, edge computing, and advanced data analytics. These innovations are almost always tied to clouds, data centers and AI foundational pillars as part of an organization’s digital business technology platform. As agencies embrace digital technologies and increase connectivity, both internally and externally, new vulnerabilities arise, exposing them to cyber threats. To mitigate these risks, cloud IT infrastructure programs must evolve alongside cloud adoption, implementing advanced security measures to stay ahead of emerging threats.

title: Design and Evaluation of a Continuous Testing Framework for Automated Front-End Validation in Student Attendance Systems
authors: N. S. Nugraha; N. A. Suwastika; I. Mulia Insan; Q. Qonita
abstract: The development of school attendance systems faces increasing challenges due to frequent updates and rapid deployment cycles, where maintaining consistent, error-resistant, and delay-free testing without affecting the production environment remains a critical issue. Addressing this problem, this paper presents the design and evaluation of an Automated Continuous Testing Framework (ACTF) for validating front-end functionalities in student attendance systems within a Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) environment. The framework integrates Cypress for end-to-end (E2E) automation and GitHub Actions for continuous execution, enabling traceable, reproducible, and scalable testing workflows. Following the Design Science Research (DSR) methodology, the study was conducted through five iterative stages: problem identification, framework design, implementation, demonstration, and evaluation. Functional requirements (FRs) were analyzed and translated into automated test scenarios using equivalence partitioning and boundary value techniques, while a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) was used to ensure comprehensive coverage between test cases and system requirements. A total of 48 automated test cases were executed across both local and cloud environments. The evaluation results demonstrated 100 % execution consistency, 100 % requirement coverage, and significantly reduced testing time compared to manual testing approaches. Furthermore, the integration of Cypress and GitHub Actions ensured continuous validation across code updates, minimizing human error and accelerating defect detection during the development process. These results confirm that the proposed framework effectively improves testing reliability, scalability, and traceability, providing a replicable model for integrating automated testing within CI/CD pipelines.
