title: The Information System Factory – Return to Simplicity
authors: W. Koch; R. Ortiz; O. Benda; A. K. Mishra
abstract: This paper presents the concept of a tool (Information System Factory) which uses a Fourth Generation Language ($\mathbf{4 G L}$) environment for the production of Information Systems in an agile Software Development Style (RAD: Rapid Application Development). The production process follows the principle of a factory, which assembles the final product by reusing already developed components and adding new components either by in house development or by acquiring external components (Component Based Development). The final system follows a three layer architecture (MVC: Model View Control) separating Data Base (Model) Management, User Interaction (View), and Programming (Control). Modern Micro Computers can be used to execute this “4GL-RAD-Tool” locally on user’s premises or in the field (powered by a battery) without the need of accessing facilities in a global network (cloud). The power of a low cost, energy saving Single Board Computer (SBC) is enough e.g. for developing and running business information systems using this tool. SBCs are frequently used in embedded Systems, which interact with sensors and actuators to control physical processes. Since SBCs can be equipped with large storage devices, there is no need in many cases to use programs in the cloud for the further on processing of big data. A realization of this 4GL-RAD Tool is based on an INFORMIX-4GL compatible system, which is available as an open source productivity tool. The System provides a menu driven IDE, which supports a standard System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as linear or iterative model. The different phases of the SDLC are delivering various artifacts like User Requirement Documents, Code, and Software User Manuals, which can be enhanced by using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Restricting the system development to classes like Business Administration, Cultural Heritage, IoT-Computing to name a few, can support the development process by introducing “domain ontologies” in the “DevOps"-Environment. The development of a Sensor Network provides a practical example in the field of Mechatronic Engineering.

title: Self Evolving AI Systems for Proactive Multi Cloud Compatibility, Resilience and Autonomous Optimization
authors: S. K. Khanday
abstract: The increasing adoption of multi-cloud architectures has introduced significant challenges in ensuring compatibility, resilience, and optimization across diverse cloud platforms. Traditional static and reactive approaches have proven inadequate for addressing the dynamic nature of multi-cloud ecosystems. This paper presents a novel self-evolving AI framework designed to proactively manage multi-cloud environments by leveraging advanced predictive models, fault-tolerant mechanisms, and optimization algorithms. The proposed framework integrates three core components: Compatibility Analyzer, Resilience Manager, and Optimization Agent, which work in tandem through an orchestration layer to ensure seamless operations. Experimental evaluations demonstrate the framework’s efficacy in achieving a $99 \%$ compatibility success rate, reducing downtime by over $65 \%$, and improving resource utilization efficiency by approximately $12 \%$ compared to baseline methods. Scalability analysis highlights the framework’s adaptability to increasing workloads, while a real-world case study validates its practical applicability. This work contributes a robust and adaptive solution for modern multi-cloud management, with potential extensions into edge computing, quantum cloud systems, and IoT-centric environments.

title: Recent Advancements in Automated Penetration Testing Tools for Web Application Security
authors: P. C. Bandhapaday; M. J. Islam; M. Saifuddin; L. Ismail; H. Salarian; S. S. Chaeikar
abstract: This paper provides a survey on the latest developments of tools for Web application security with a comprehensive assessment of eight published studies from 2020 to 2025 – insight into their efficiency, how much they are integrated into artificial intelligence (AI), and regulations such as PCI DSS/GDPR. Improvements in the detection of well-known flaws are evident, as demonstrated by Burp Suite reaching 70%+ coverage of OWASP Top 10 risks and OWASP ZAP with the best cost-effective scanning at this post from a set of tools including AI-driven frameworks such as the Intelligent Automated Penetration Testing System (IAPTS). The MDDQN (relational) algorithm shows promising results in few-shot adversarial robustness via acceleration of attack path planning from reinforcement learning and deep neural networks for efficiency. Still, some are quite challenging, e.g., high computational costs, misidentifications, and inability to detect zero-days necessitate the motivations for hybrid approaches combining automated and manual testing. Reviewed studies stress the critical need for evolving threats tackled by multi-tool strategies and integrations in continues integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines for ongoing testing. Regulatory compliance is important, so tools to allow the regular upgrades of compliance will be useful. Investigation directions should focus on establishing benchmarks, lowering the barriers to implementation of AI, and improving detection of advanced attacks. Through synthesis of technical developments and practitioner experiences, this research aimed to improve the comprehension of automated penetration testing capabilities in securing web apps from evolving cyberattacks as of 2025.
keywords: automated penetration testing;web application security;ethical hacking;AI-driven testing;vulnerability assessment;compliance

title: How Do Developers Use ChatGPT for Software Test Generation? Usage Patterns, Satisfaction, and Code Adoption Analysis
authors: S. He; W. Zhan; J. Wang; J. Dai; H. Chen; C. Tan; F. Li
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT are increasingly used by developers to generate test code, yet little is known about their real-world usage patterns, developer satisfaction, and the extent to which generated code is integrated into software projects. This paper presents an empirical study of 407 user-ChatGPT conversations related to test generation from GitHub, including 152 that contain both test and corresponding source code. We systematically categorize the primary use cases of ChatGPT in test generation, employ sentiment analysis to assess developer satisfaction across different testing scenarios, and analyze the adoption between ChatGPT-generated test code and existing project code using PMD’s Copy-Paste Detector (CPD) tool. Our analysis identifies six ChatGPT usage scenarios in test generation: test case creation, framework demonstration, test enhancement, debugging, CI/CD integration, and mocking solution. Among these, test case creation and framework demonstration emerge as the most frequent. Sentiment analysis reveals that, except for framework demonstration, all other scenarios exhibit a higher proportion of negative feedback than positive. Moreover, adoption analysis indicates that only 25.7% of conversations show evidence of code reuse, suggesting developers are generally cautious when integrating LLM-generated test code. Based on these findings, we propose several practical implications for enhancing the effectiveness of LLM-assisted test generation.

title: AutoDrift: A Forecast-Aware Concept Drift Detection and Retraining Pipeline in MLOps with CMAPSS
authors: R. K. Myakala; P. K. Nagata; S. Lavudya; S. K. Pedhapally; V. R. Podduturi
abstract: Concept drift poses a critical challenge to deploying reliable machine learning models in real-world production environments, particularly in time series forecasting and predictive maintenance systems. We present AutoDrift, a modular, forecast-aware framework to detect concept drift and trigger the automated retraining of models within modern MLOps pipelines. This approach integrates Facebook Prophet for time series prediction, statistical drift detection techniques such as the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test, and Apache Airflow to orchestrate retraining and deployment tasks in response to detected drift. Using the widely bench marked NASA CMAPSS dataset, we simulate real-world engine degradation and sensor drift conditions to evaluate AutoDrift's effectiveness in predictive maintenance scenarios. The results demonstrate that AutoDrift maintains high forecasting accuracy (91 % precision) while reducing retraining latency by 37 % compared to static retraining schedules. The framework supports model versioning via MLflow and is cloud-agnostic, enabling seamless deployment across Kubernetes, AWS, and on-premises environments. AutoDrift offers a practical solution to one of the most pressing MLOps challenges such as maintaining the adaptability of deployed models to changing data distributions, by unifying drift detection, retraining logic, and orchestration in a single, extensible pipeline. The system is designed to be interpretable, scalable, and easy to integrate into existing machine learning operations, making it suitable for industrial applications in aviation, IoT, and large-scale telemetry monitoring.

title: CyberHeraclius: Cyber Defence Evaluation Methodology
authors: G. Hatzivasilis; S. Ioannidis
abstract: Security evaluation remains a critical challenge in cybersecurity, especially with the growing complexity of systems like cloud and IoT environments. This paper introduces CyberHeraclius, a novel methodology for evaluating the security of modern computer networks. The process begins with automated asset mapping and the collection of public Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) from MITRE’s CVE, CWE, and CAPEC repositories, as well as Metasploit. To address CTI limitations, such as false positives and coverage gaps, automated penetration testing is used to verify actual vulnerabilities. The validated results feed into a Medieval Castle-based security model, which assesses system resilience based on component composition. CTI risk metrics are then integrated with the model’s aggregation formulas to quantify overall system risk. CyberHeraclius is part of the SecOPERA Platform, which supports secure continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines for system developers.

title: Applying DevOps and DaaS in the Smart Laboratory of Internet of Things
authors: I. Izotov; N. Papulovskaya
abstract: This paper presents the results of developing a Smart Laboratory. The Smart Laboratory is a platform for remotely developing embedded system software. It enables remote access to physical hardware for software development, testing, and deployment on microcontroller-based devices. The creation of the online laboratory involved several key tasks: designing a network infrastructure to integrate laboratory equipment into a unified system, developing a web application for remote interaction with microcontrollers, implementing a digital twin of the test module for flexible configuration and management, and conducting testing and validation. During development, a hypothesis emerged that the combination of DevOps and Device as a Service (DaaS) opens new possibilities for automated IoT device management. The DaaS concept enables on-demand remote access to physical devices, while the DevOps methodology facilitated the automation of user software deployment. A compilation and delivery pipeline for firmware updates was implemented to support this process. Ansible was utilized to automate software updates on Raspberry Pi testbed computers. Prometheus was employed for metric collection, and Grafana was used for data visualization, ensuring system performance monitoring. The platform was tested and validated at the Institute of Radio Electronics and Information Technologies - RTF (UrFU). The invention has been patented.

title: IoT-Enabled Water Quality Monitoring with Auto-Scalable Cloud DevOps Pipelines
authors: T. B; R. G. K.A; R. G
abstract: IoT-Enabled Water Quality Monitoring with Auto-Scalable Cloud DevOps Pipelines introduces AquaGuardian, a distributed Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud-integrated platform designed for ongoing assessment of important water quality parameters, including pH, temperature, turbidity, and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS). The system uses ESP32 microcontrollers connected to environmental sensors to capture real-time measurements and send them securely to AWS IoT Core with the MQTT protocol. The incoming data is stored in cloud services like Amazon DynamoDB and Amazon S3, where it is further examined to spot anomalies in water quality. When the system detects abnormal readings, it automatically sends user notifications through AWS Simple Notification Service (SNS) via SMS or email. To support scalable, reliable, and automated deployment, AquaGuardian incorporates a CAI/CD DevOps pipeline using GitHub, AWS CodePipeline, and AWS Lambda. This setup allows for continuous updates and operational efficiency. The solution offers real-time insights, high reliability, and less need for human intervention, making it ideal for large-scale smart water monitoring applications.

title: Forging Industry 5.0 DevOps: Towards Secure and Scalable OT Orchestration Powered by Kubernetes
authors: N. Giulianelli; A. Sabbioni; S. Montebugnoli; A. Bujari; A. Corradi
abstract: The ongoing digitization of Operational Technology (OT) and the integration of Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) devices are fundamentally transforming modern industrial systems. However, the heterogeneity of hardware and software ecosystems amplifies the complexity of this transformation, making orchestration and lifecycle management especially challenging. To address these challenges, modern DevOps practices—such as Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD), runtime observability, and fine-grained access control—are essential. These practices help accelerate time-to-market, maintain service quality, manage operational complexity, and uphold security standards. Advancing toward seamless integration of OT within cloud-native environments, we introduce a prototype Orchestrator based on the Kubernetes plarform, aimed at providing a comprehensive lifecycle management for OT devices in industrial contexts. Our proposal bridges the traditional divide between IT and OT by seamlessly integrating with existing CI/CD pipelines and implementing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) tailored to device-level permissions. Through a unified abstraction layer, it simplifies the management of heterogeneous, multi-vendor hardware, enabling scalable, secure, and efficient operations across diverse industrial deployments.

title: Current Challenges and Future Perspectives in Testing IoT Systems: A Comprehensive Review
authors: B. Lima; R. Pinto
abstract: The widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) systems in domains like healthcare, manufacturing, and smart cities has brought new challenges for software and systems testing. This survey systematically reviews studies published from 2012, identifying key testing types, methods, and tools across the IoT stack. Our analysis highlights sensor-specific challenges—including timing jitter, calibration drift, and environmental coupling—that remain underexplored in prior surveys. We propose a multidimensional conceptual framework that cross-correlates architectural layers, testing objectives, and technology targets, enabling structured comparison of testing strategies. The framework is empirically validated through an industrial case study, which reveals critical gaps, such as a lack of cross-layer coverage, limited tool support for real-time constraints, and inadequate mechanisms for sensor fault resilience. We conclude by outlining future research directions, including digital twin-based validation, unified IoT testing pipelines, and lightweight security testing for constrained devices. This work provides researchers and practitioners with a sensor-aware, empirically grounded roadmap for advancing IoT testing.

abstract: IT organization, nowadays, are following manual process for doing code review process, Developers submits the pull request or merge request in tool. title: Integrating Security into CI/CD Pipelines: A DevOps Approach to Application Deployment
authors: S. N. V; R. S. B; J. Sathiamoorthy
abstract: The recent blistering shift in the direction of the DevOps practices and Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment pipelines has changed the process of software delivery and development. However, these dynamic approaches have also resulted in the creation of new attack surfaces and security threats. The dynamic and time sensitive aspect of the modern software delivery cannot fit in the perimeter centered security models. The following paper will present my DevOps-powered security integration platform or, to be more specific, DevSecOps which is the composite of security control and vulnerability scanning alongside confirmation that CI/CD pipelines meet the standards. This may enable development teams to identify and address vulnerabilities earlier in the software life cycle and mitigate their exposure to risk as well as enable them to release their software more quickly by shifting security to the left. The architecture contained in our proposed scheme presents an architecture that is tool independent and converts the benefits, both performance and security, to a real life deployment scenario.

title: Implementation of CI/CD in Industrial Automation
authors: V. S. Oleynikov; E. V. Zhdamirova; O. S. Aleksandrova
abstract: This paper presents an approach to implementing CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) methodology in industrial automation, based on the O-PAS (Open Process Automation Standard) for ensuring compatibility, scalability, and security of control systems. A practical architecture is proposed for automated software deployment on a well pad using virtual PLCs, SCADA systems, and a centralized decision-making center. The study analyzes potential benefits, challenges, and risks associated with such an implementation, focusing on cybersecurity, network resilience, and the use of open-source virtualized components. The proposed solution can significantly reduce deployment time, improve system maintainability, and simplify scaling of automated industrial facilities.

title: Optimizing Cloud Cost and Compliance in Azure DevOps Pipelines for Industrial Applications
authors: S. N. Donthi
abstract: More and more, manufacturers are using Cloud DevOps pipelines for integration and deployment. When pipelines are imperfect, they can cause a high cloud cost. And it can also lead to compliance violations. This is especially true in regulated industries. Our framework aims to optimize Azure DevOps pipeline (cost and compliance). Resource scheduling is one of the techniques. The self-hosted agents, Infrastructure as Code policies and automatic compliance checks are also features of it. According to an industrial IoT application case study, the suggested approach reduces the cloud costs from $12,500 /month to $8,750/month (30 % Reduction). The number of regulatory breaches has dropped from 100 to 50 per day. Construction time has also dropped from 25 to 23 minutes. By complying with the rules and regulations of DevOps activities, the proposed plan can help industries in saving monetary values.

title: AI for DevSecOps Optimization: Investigating the Role of AI/ML in Predictive Vulnerability Detection During CI/CD Pipeline Stages
authors: T. Kalwani
abstract: In this paper, the focus is placed on the integration of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into the CI/CD pipelines of DevSecOps for predictive vulnerability detection. A specially selected dataset of 416 past code commits and vulnerability reports was used for the model building of the Random Forest and Recurrent Neural Network models. The designed AI-based system was seen to reach a detection accuracy of up to 93.8%, greatly outperforming the results yielded by conventional static code analysis solutions yet achieving a latency decrease of over 83%, as measured across repeated CI/CD build cycles in the associated security scan. With predictive models directly integrated into the CI/CD pipeline, the system allows for real-time and context-aware security reviews and the decrease of false positives, ultimately boosting the productivity of developers and the deployment time.
